sections.normalized_html:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of [MATH: y=\sin x.]

  • Then, reflect it in the [MATH: x]-axis to give [MATH: y=-\sin x.]

  • Finally, stretch it parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis by a stretch factor of [MATH: 8] to give [MATH: y=-8\sin x.]

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of [MATH: y=-8\sin x.]

items.title: Identifying the Reflection of a Sine or Cosine Curve Over the Vertical Axis

sections.normalized_html: The graph above shows the function [MATH: y=2\sin(kx).] What is the value of [MATH: k?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/643d638672fe9059c6151e7469aa87c1]

The graph above shows the function [MATH: y=2\sin(kx).] What is the value of [MATH: k?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of [MATH: y=\sin x.]

  • Then, reflect it across the [MATH: y]-axis.

  • Finally, stretch it parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis by a stretch factor of [MATH: 2.]

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of [MATH: y=2\sin(-x).] Hence, [MATH: k=-1.]

Notice that, because the sine function is odd, the [MATH: y]-axis reflection has the same effect as the [MATH: x]-axis reflection, i.e.,

[MATH: 2\sin(-x) = -2\sin x .]

So the graph could also be viewed as [MATH: y=-2\sin x.]
